demonstration.narration: Checkout is reported slow. I'll keep only requests that took at least two seconds, so fast traffic doesn't get in the way.
demonstration.reasoning: The window holds normal events as well as the problem. Filtering on ${var.field} removes that noise, so we can look at the records that matter.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted event.duration column now holds only requests of two seconds or more. ${param.fault.chain} all report a delay at least that long, so it is being passed along the checkout path. One of them can show where it starts.

demonstration.narration: I'll open one slow request from the deepest service on that path. Its service, operation and duration show where the delay starts.
demonstration.reasoning: A total can look convincing even when it includes other records. Opening one typical event shows the key values together, which a count alone can't do.
demonstration.evidence: This slow request belongs to ${truth.finding}, on GET ${truth.scope}, and took about ${param.delay.seconds} seconds (event.duration counts nanoseconds). That's the same delay the services calling it report. It's the deepest service on the path, so it's where the delay starts.
